Emma Chen: Quick sync — we need a final PRD+launch checklist for the serving runtime changes (attention scheduling, kernel packing heuristics, and KV memoization). Customer asks are piling up, want to align scope before Monday.
Raj Patel: I can draft the RFC but need clear acceptance criteria from product/CS. Do we gate on latency, p95 tail, correctness?
Mei Lin: For attention scheduling we should measure both throughput and per-request p99. Memoization (KV-level caching) will change cache hit semantics — need migration plan for warm vs cold requests.
Emma Chen: Primary customer asks: (1) deterministic latencies for 7k-8k seqs under dedicated; (2) no correctness regressions for generation; (3) ability to pin older kernel variant per model. Marcus, can you confirm wording?
Marcus Ruiz: Yup. Enterprise customer A requires <350ms median for 2k context and <1s p95 for 8k on dedicated. They also need audit log entries when kernel variant switches.
Olya S.: Ops note — audit logs + rollout traces are fine, but we need feature-flag hooks and an emergency rollback path that doesn't require model reupload.
Raj Patel: Proposal for rollout: 1) internal perf regression tests (bench-suite), 2) canary at 5% traffic with shadowing to baseline, 3) gated ramp to 50% then 100%. Canary must record kernel choice per request.
Mei Lin: Bench-suite should include microbench + end-to-end traces with KV memoization on/off. Also include synthetic interleaved short+long seq patterns to catch fragmentation/packing regressions.
Emma Chen: Acceptance criteria draft (for PRD):
```
- No correctness regressions on canonical eval set (exact-match + logprob divergence thresholds)
- Latency SLOs: median <350ms (2k), p95 <1s (8k) on dedicated baseline hw
- Token-throughput delta <= 15% (batching enabled) or cost per token not worse than baseline by >15%
- Telemetry: kernel_variant + kv_hit_rate + memoization_evictions emitted per request
- Rollback: automatic fallback to baseline kernel in <60s if p95 increases by >25% during canary
```
Raj Patel: Additions: compatibility matrix for quantized models and CUDA drivers; a KMS-safe path for private deployments (no telemetry leak).
Marcus Ruiz: Also add 'customer pinning API' to the PRD: allow customer to override server routing to `kernel:v1` for selected deployment. Need docs + API contract.
Olya S.: Edge cases: 1) KV memoization bloom filter false positives causing stale responses — need TTL semantics on memoized entries; 2) packed-kernel out-of-memory for extreme batch combos — add quota/backpressure.
Mei Lin: For TTLs I propose `memo_ttl_ms` per-model default 600000 (10min) and a `memo_strict_consistency` flag for regulated customers (disables memoization for safety).
Emma Chen: Good. Who owns what? Raj — RFC and perf-suite. Mei — telemetry schema + bench harness. Olya — rollout automation + runbook. Marcus — customer communication + pin API spec.
Raj Patel: Will put RFC up by EOD Fri. Need an API stub for pinning to reference in docs.
Marcus Ruiz: I'll draft the customer email template and include the migration note about potential cold-start flakiness during first 24h.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: new RFC draft posted: /rfc/serving/runtime-atten-pack-memoization-172945. Link: https://redwood.internal/rfc/172945
Emma Chen: :thumbsup: Please keep PRD tiny — we can split follow-ups into ops-only and compliance-only. Next sync Tue 10am to sign off launch criteria.
